disposition_reason: Table I gives quarterly mean ± SD of lead, chromium, cadmium, nickel, copper and cobalt by AAS in onion, spinach, lettuce, cucumber and pineapple bought at Kaura Namoda central market.

study.design: seasonal market monitoring, one vendor, four quarterly purchases
study.market: Kaura Namoda central market, Zamfara State, Nigeria (same vendors each quarter)
study.period_text: December 2024, and March, June and September 2025 (quarterly)
study.method: flame AAS after HCl-HNO3 (3:1) hot-plate digestion of oven-dried powder
study.qa: instrument calibration and triplicate analysis only; no CRM or recovery

controls.outcome: Paper reports highest metal levels in Q1 (December, dry season), then Q4, lowest in Q3 (June, rainy season), ANOVA p < 0.05; e.g. spinach lead 0.08 (Q1) vs 0.007 mg/kg (Q3), cucumber lead 0.18 (Q1) vs 0.00 (Q2)

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Permissible lead limit cited for vegetables

unresolved: Number of units bought per quarter is not stated; values are triplicate analytical means.

Text and abstract conflict with Table I: abstract says cucumber Pb 0.18 mg/kg in Q4 (table: Q1); text says cucumber Cu 0.17 in Q1 (table 0.47; Co is 0.17) and Ni 0.35 in Q3 (table 0.32); text says lettuce Q2 metals were all below detection (table prints values). Table I values recorded as printed.
Figure 3 titled spinach displays the pineapple Q1 values.
The text refers to a Table II for cucumber and pineapple that is not printed separately; values are in Table I.
